import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_78/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_78/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_78/training_2.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source3_78_0 and Source3_78_2 on movie_id
df0_2 = pd.merge(df0, df2[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Operation 2: group_by [Source3_78_0.movie_id, Source3_78_2.title], aggregations = avg(Source3_78_0.rating)
grouped_0_2 = df0_2.groupby(['movie_id', 'title'], as_index=False)['rating'].mean()
grouped_0_2.rename(columns={'rating': 'avg_rating'}, inplace=True)

# Operation 3: JOIN Source3_78_0 and Source3_78_1 on user_id
df0_1 = pd.merge(df0, df1[['user_id', 'sex']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Operation 4: group_by [Source3_78_0.movie_id, Source3_78_2.title], aggregations = avg(Source3_78_0.rating)
# We need to join df0_1 with df2 to get title for grouping
df0_1_2 = pd.merge(df0_1, df2[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Group by movie_id, title, and sex to get average rating per sex
grouped_0_1_2 = df0_1_2.groupby(['movie_id', 'title', 'sex'], as_index=False)['rating'].mean()

# Operation 5: group_by [Source3_78_0.movie_id, Source3_78_2.title], aggregations = avg(Source3_78_0.rating)
# This operation is repeated, so no new action needed beyond above.

# Operation 6: PIVOT
# Pivot the grouped data to have columns 'F' and 'M' for average ratings by sex
pivot_df = grouped_0_1_2.pivot(index=['movie_id', 'title'], columns='sex', values='rating').reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema
pivot_df.rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'}, inplace=True)

# The target schema is ['movie_id': int, 'title': str, 'F': float, 'M': float]
# Ensure correct dtypes
pivot_df['movie_id'] = pivot_df['movie_id'].astype(int)
pivot_df['title'] = pivot_df['title'].astype(str)
pivot_df['F'] = pivot_df['F'].astype(float)
pivot_df['M'] = pivot_df['M'].astype(float)

# Save the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_78/target_multisource.csv"
pivot_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 as instructed
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_78/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_78/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_78/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_78_0 and Source3_78_1 on user_id
df = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_78_2 on movie_id
df = pd.merge(df, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by movie_id, title, sex and aggregate average rating
grouped = df.groupby(["movie_id", "title", "sex"], as_index=False).agg({"rating": "mean"})

# Pivot the sex column to get separate columns for F and M with average ratings
pivoted = grouped.pivot(index=["movie_id", "title"], columns="sex", values="rating").reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
pivoted = pivoted.rename(columns={"F": "F", "M": "M"})

# Ensure columns order as in target schema
pivoted = pivoted[["movie_id", "title", "F", "M"]]

# Write output to the specified file
pivoted.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_78/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
